subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a knight model as a single TypeScript module, thinking through which SDK primitives to use—builder, joints, chains, sweeps, extrusion, lathe—plus textures and paint for a griffin emblem, aiming for something well-structured but not overly long.

I'm working out the figure's anatomy: standing upright facing forward at roughly 1.9m, with a joint hierarchy rooted at the hips branching into spine/neck/head and limb chains for arms and legs. I'm also figuring out how the chain API's naming convention maps spans to joint names, making sure each limb path gets the right number of names including the tip joint.

For the torso and armor, I'm deciding to keep things simple with boxes, cylinders, and lathed shapes rather than complex lofting, since the art direction favors blocky primitives. Parts will attach to bones with explicit positions in model space, keeping rotations simple since static geometry just inherits its bone's orientation. For the surcoat I'm leaning toward solid color rather than stripes.

For battle wear I'm thinking of mottled steel textures to suggest dirt and wear, and considering an svg texture approach for a griffin emblem on the shoulder plates—sketching it as simple shapes (ellipse body, circle head, wing paths, beak). Since grey-toned drawings get tinted by the part's base color, I could draw the griffin in greys and set the part color to white to get a silver effect, though I still need to work out how the blue surcoat background interacts with that texture.

I'm settling on a color svg with a blue background and silver griffin so it displays its own colors directly, applied to a plane or thin box positioned as the tabard front. For the kite shield, I'm orienting the extrusion so its face points forward along the z-axis with thickness in that direction, then planning to add the griffin decal as a slightly offset textured plane on the shield's front face.

For the heads, I'm sketching a lathe-based great helm with a dark eye slit box and a crimson feathered plume extruded vertically and positioned at the top-back, considering how to orient it in the YZ plane so it sweeps backward naturally.

Next I'm planning the cape as a jagged, torn-edge extrusion hanging behind the shoulders in crimson, then moving to the sword with a thin diamond-profile blade, box cross guard, cylindrical grip, and spherical pommel held in the knight's right hand (negative X side) pointing down toward the floor. For shoulder pauldrons, I'm considering scaled sphere geometry to create layered dome shapes.Next, I'm planning a torn crimson cape as a thin extruded shape hanging behind the shoulders with jagged tattered edges, and a sword with a diamond-profile blade pointing downward in the knight's right hand, complete with a box cross-guard, cylindrical grip, and spherical pommel. For the pauldrons, I'm considering scaled spheres layered to form rounded shoulder armor.

Now I'm detailing the dome pauldron using a hemisphere sphere geometry, adding gold torus trim rings for filigree, and applying a mottled steel paint texture for dents and wear, then exploring using a gold scrollwork SVG texture mapped onto the hemisphere's UVs for added detail.

With the budget in mind, I'm planning to keep part count around 60-80 and now sketching the skeleton structure, starting with a hip root joint and building a spine chain through catmull-rom path points up toward a neck and head joint.

I'm reconsidering this approach though—going with a simpler setup: explicit parent-child joints plus limb-style chains for arms and legs, with rigid parts for other pieces. Now I'm working out the shoulder, elbow, and wrist chain for the left arm, parenting it to the upper spine joint, and double-checking that the chain's path points and names array line up correctly.

I'm mirroring this for the right arm using a sign-flipped side variable, then setting up the hip, knee, and ankle chains for both legs in the same loop, making sure every joint name gets a unique side suffix. With the skeleton structured, I'm moving on to defining the armor color palette—steel, gold, crimson, blue, silver, leather, and eye tones—for the parts I'll attach next.

Now I'm defining a helper function to simplify creating parts with geometry, color, bone attachment, and position, then building the chest piece as a lathe-shaped breastplate with a barrel-like profile, painted with a weathered steel mottle effect for battle wear, followed by starting a blue tabard plane to drape over the front of the torso.

I'm reworking the surcoat approach -- instead of a separate flat tabard plane that would be hidden by the armor lathe, I'm making the surcoat itself a blue lathe shape covering the torso at a slightly larger radius than the armor, from waist to chest height, so it drapes over the breastplate convincingly.

Rigging the legs now, with hip/knee/ankle joints positioned and tapered cylinder geometry for the thighs using direction vectors to orient each segment correctly along the limb.

Continuing down to shins and sabaton boots, then adding a belt with a buckle at the pelvis before moving on to the arms—upper arm and forearm as tapered cylinders between shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints, with sphere joints for elbow cops and boxes for gauntlets at the wrists.

Now I'm designing the pauldrons as layered hemisphere shells at the shoulders, considering gold filigree texturing on the top layer, then working out the gorget as a short cylinder ring at the neck and a great helm built from a lathed profile with a dark visor slit box at the front.

For the helm I'm adding a faceplate box over the face with a cut slit, a nose guard bar, and now shaping a crimson plume extrusion on top—thin in the X direction so it reads as a narrow crest, sitting on the helm's crown and sweeping upward like horsehair.

Now I'm working out the kite shield for the left arm, held forward at the side, defining its outline in cross-section with a flat top and a sharp pointed bottom, extruded along X for thickness.

I'm positioning the shield so it clears the torso surface without intersecting, then adding the heraldic decal plane in front of it—sized to match the shield outline with a blue field and silver griffin design, computing the plane's offset and center to align with the shield's shape.

Mapping the kite silhouette's vertices into SVG coordinate space, then working out which direction the plane's local axes correspond to in world space so the heraldry faces correctly outward from the shield.

Not going to overanalyze the mirroring further — I'll just draw the griffin facing left in the SVG and call it symmetric enough for a heraldic shield look. Now I'm sketching the griffin shape itself: a silver-grey body with blue background field, building out the ellipse body, circular head, beak, wings, tail, and legs as simple geometric shapes.

Still writing SVG code...

For the surcoat/tabard version I'll reuse the same griffin shape but wrap it in a different viewBox and plane size, though the aspect ratios don't quite match between the shield and tabard proportions, so I need to think about how to handle that mismatch.

I'm working through placement for the cape (torn crimson cloth draped from the shoulders with a jagged torn bottom edge), then designing the sword as separate parts: pommel, grip, crossguard, and a tapered blade extruded sideways, all positioned relative to the right hand's existing arm chain.

Now I'm deciding how to add wear details like dents and scratches using surface-based decal placement, and planning the pauldron shoulder armor as a layered dome with gold filigree texture over an opaque steel backing so the geometry isn't accidentally cut away by transparency.

I'm laying out the rest of the armor pieces — knee and elbow spheres, gauntlets, boots — and then defining the skeleton joint hierarchy from hips up through spine, neck, and head, followed by the arm chains running from shoulder to elbow to wrist.

Still defining joint chains...

I'm sorting out the leg chain from hip to ankle, then confirming how roles and bones attach parts to the skeleton, and listing out the color palette and paint textures (mottled steel, blade steel, mottled crimson for the cape) I'll need.

Writing SVG code...

I'm designing the griffin emblem as an SVG overlay — wings, body, head, beak, and tail shapes in silver with dark outlines — meant to sit on both the kite shield (with a blue kite-shaped background) and the tabard (with a blue rectangular background), sized to match each plane's aspect ratio.

Writing filigree SVG pattern...

I'm working out the surcoat's lathe profile so it flares into a skirt covering the thighs down to around knee height, then adding a leather belt with a gold buckle and a steel gorget collar at the neck.

Now I'm detailing the helm: a lathe-shaped dome, a faceplate, a nose guard, an eye slit split on either side of the nose guard, and starting on a trailing plume extrude for the crest.

Writing plume outline points...

I'm laying out the plume's extrude profile as a sweeping fin trailing backward and upward from the helm's crown, then shifting to the kite shield's extrude outline with a pointed bottom tip, deciding it should be held via the left wrist bone with a forward-facing dome boss mounted on its face.

Now I'm working through the sword — blade extrude oriented sideways, a crossguard spanning front-to-back, a leather-wrapped grip, and a gold pommel — positioning it near the left hand's wrist joint.
